reasoning: The only state-specific general-election polling in the last 45 days that directly measures California’s 2026 electorate is for the gubernatorial race: several reports summarize a UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies poll showing Democrat Xavier Becerra leading Republican Steve Hilton statewide by roughly the high-teens to mid-20s, depending on the specific release cited.[2][7][11] These are not Senate or presidential polls and must be treated as separate context, but they reinforce the underlying Democratic strength already reflected in California’s strongly Democratic Cook Partisan Voting Index (around D+18 statewide).[1] I found no reputable, state-specific general-election polling for a 2026 California U.S. Senate race or for a 2026 presidential general-election margin in California within the last 45 days, so I cannot state a current numeric D+ or R+ margin for those races based on new data; structurally, both contests remain heavily advantaged for Democrats but without fresh, race-specific polling to quantify that advantage.
